strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#64158 by building pandas from source at the buggy commit 5c74f126aa1e (meson-python editable build with --no-build-isolation) and running the PR's new out-of-bounds-ordinal tests. On the buggy revision the overflowing nanosecond ordinal is silently replaced by 0 (1970 epoch), so pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime) should report DID NOT RAISE. On the fixed revision the same tests should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with the expected message. Success is that transition only; no values are compared numerically.

system_packages: a C compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) and a C++ compiler, needed by the Cython/meson build
build_commands: python -m pip install cython meson-python meson ninja

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy 5c74f126aa1e: the listed out_of_bounds_ordinal tests fail, each because pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime) sees no exception (the call returns 1970-epoch periods). On the fixed revision (PR head, rebuilt): all of them pass, because the call raises OutOfBoundsDatetime with the message 'Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 2300-01-01' (or the matching year/unit for the other cases).
risks: The fix lives in Cython and C (period.pyx and np_datetime.c). After checking out the fixed revision the editable build must be rebuilt; a stale build reproduces the buggy result on the fixed tree.

Cython version is not documented and the era table is unbounded. Pick the Cython 3.x that the revision's pyproject build-system requires, and record the version used. Cython's noexcept handling is what produces the swallowed exception.
The fixed revision's commit SHA is not in the context (only the PR number). The PR head SHA must be obtained before the fixed run can be done.

The buggy-side failure mode (DID NOT RAISE) is inferred from the description, not observed directly. If the buggy tree raises some other error, the transition is still expected but the message differs.

Platform: the overflow is int64 nanosecond arithmetic, so it should reproduce on 64-bit Linux and macOS. Windows needs tzdata and was not evidenced. 32-bit platforms are untested and may not behave identically.
The reproducing tests filter pandas.errors.Pandas4Warning by name. If that class does not exist at the buggy commit, pytest will error at collection rather than fail on the assertion.
pandas' pytest configuration may turn warnings into errors. The 'Exception ignored in' message goes to stderr rather than the warnings system, so it should not itself change the outcome.

The tz_convert test change (to_period_ns case expecting 'Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp') is a message change tied to GH#66550, and the PR body is truncated about that expectation. It is excluded from the reproducing command for that reason.
The test_construction_extreme_years_never_silent test uses extreme years such as 2**31-1 and may be slow or hit unrelated errors, so it is excluded from the command.
No Python version is stated in the evidence. Use a Python version the revision supports (3.11 or 3.12 is a reasonable choice) and record it.
Boundary years for nanosecond bounds are not given beyond the 2300 example, so the strategy relies only on the explicit 2300, 1600 and 300000 cases.

oracle.reference_source: PR #66829 test diff (exception type and message match)
oracle.why: The check is whether OutOfBoundsDatetime is raised with a matching message. No numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime) sees no exception, because the overflow was discarded and the call returned 1970-epoch periods, so the test fails with DID NOT RAISE.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed code validates bounds before converting and raises OutOfBoundsDatetime with the expected 'Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp' message, so the pytest.raises block is satisfied.
